newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee shade up on sale of dollars.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee shade up on sale of dollars.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee edged up early on Tuesday as a foreign bank sold dollars, but dealers said they expected the currency to move in a narrow range during the day.

At 0445 GMT the rupee was at 57.22 to the dollar after opening at its previous closing level of 57.25. "The early gain in the rupee was due to aggressive selling of dollars by a foreign bank," said an American Express Bank dealer.

But movement would remain in a range, with the downside of the exchange rate cushioned by banks using low call rates to build dollar positions, and the upside at near the Central Bank top, said a Citibank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar by a quarter local cent, despite substantial easing overseas against the yen, dealers said. Buying and selling prices were fixed at 56.1825 and 57.3125.
"The Central Bank action is also an indication they are comfortable with the current exchange rate," said the American Express dealer.
Overnight call money was at 12.5 percent, after opening at 13 percent, they said.
